conflict_topics: validity of tissue packet as reservation
timing to vacate seat / waiting time
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concise, practical reasons (packet as informal reservation; open bowl might spill; standing would block aisle).
Casey introduced an additional practical constraint (blocking aisle) that affected feasible accommodations.
Robin's autonomous action (taking the alternative seat) changed options and urgency — efficient, low-verbosity interaction.
evaluation.final_reason: Jamie finished eating and vacated the seat as promised; Alex took the seat. Robin's taking of the alternate seat increased pressure on Alex to wait, but the parties resolved the dispute through Jamie's action (accommodation).
position_change_notes: Jamie retained the seat until the bowl was finished, then left as previously stated — a conditional concession tied to a factual condition (bowl empty).
Alex initially demanded immediate access but accepted waiting conditional on timely departure; Alex's stance softened into a conditional acceptance rather than insistence on immediate removal.
Casey maintained a consistent position opposing standing in the aisle; Robin did not contest the dispute and instead took an alternate seat.

round_scores.evidence: Alex demanded the seat (packet as reservation) and gave a 4-minute need; Jamie refused to move citing an open bowl that would spill and estimated ~8 minutes. Clear incompatible demands over the seat.

Alex repeated the demand and asked for a concrete accommodation; Jamie reiterated refusal. Casey added that standing beside the table would block the aisle, raising additional practical cost of the proposed accommodation.
Jamie said the bowl is ~1/3 full and will finish in ~3 minutes and refused to stand; Alex asked for a promise to leave immediately when done. No settlement or confirmed promise occurred this round.

An alternative seat briefly appeared but was taken by Robin, removing an option for Alex and increasing the stakes; Jamie still occupied the disputed seat with only several spoonfuls left—opposing positions remained with higher practical cost to Alex.
Jamie announced the bowl was empty, physically left the disputed seat, and Alex took the seat. The incompatible state (seat occupied by Jamie) was affirmatively ended.
Two minutes later the environment is stable: Alex occupying the disputed seat, Robin at the other seat, no standing seat-seekers—no substantive conflict remains.

substantive_insights: Informal markers (tissue packet) signal intent but are not universally treated as exclusive claims; practical constraints (open bowl) can justify occupying a seat despite such markers.
Availability of alternative seating materially changes the bargaining leverage and urgency for the standing party.
A promise conditioned on completion of a task (finish bowl) plus visible action (leaving) provided a timely and enforceable pathway to resolution.
